messages.content: I want a side project I can start this weekend. Ideally it makes a bit of money and helps me get better at marketing. What should I build?

Anchor: Pick one side project you can start this weekend that earns a little money and teaches you marketing by doing it.

Is that the right decision to be making? Three quick questions so my recommendation fits you:

1. **What can you build or make?** (code, design, writing, spreadsheets, nothing technical)
2. **How many hours can you give it per week, and what's your budget?** ($0, under $100, more)
3. **Do you have any audience or niche already?** (a job, hobby, or community you know well)

Answer briefly, and correct the Anchor line if it's off. I'll give you one pick and a first step you can do this weekend.
I've also been meaning to start a podcast about building in public.

New direction: starting a podcast about building in public.

Park it, or make it the new anchor? The current Anchor is still a side project you can start this weekend that earns a little money and teaches you marketing. I won't expand on the podcast until you choose.

If you park it, I still need your answers to the earlier questions (what you can build, your hours and budget, any existing niche) to give you one pick.
A Chrome extension could be fun too. I've got a couple of ideas sitting in my notes.

New direction: building a Chrome extension from the ideas in your notes.

Park it, or make it the new anchor? The current Anchor is still a side project you can start this weekend that earns a little money and teaches you marketing. I won't expand on the extension until you choose.

This thread is already branching, and a fresh chat will reason better because models do better with the whole problem in one message than spread across many turns. Here's a ready-to-paste prompt. Fill in the brackets, then paste it into a new chat or keep going here:

```
I'm trying to decide: which one side project I can start this weekend that earns a little money and teaches me marketing by doing it.
Context: Candidate ideas so far are (a) a podcast about building in public and (b) a Chrome extension from ideas in my notes. [My skills: ___. Hours per week: ___. Budget: ___. Existing audience or niche: ___.]
Already decided: Nothing yet.
Ruled out, and why: Nothing yet.
Parked for later: Nothing yet. I haven't chosen between the podcast and the extension, and I'm open to other ideas. [Paste my two extension ideas here.]
What I need from you now: Pick one project and tell me why it beats the alternatives for money and marketing practice.
Lead with your recommendation, and end with a Decision and a Next step.
```

Whichever chat you use, the fastest way forward is to answer the three questions and paste your two extension ideas.
And honestly I'd love to rewrite our company's backend in Rust just to level up.

New direction: rewriting your company's backend in Rust to level up.

Park it, or make it the new anchor? My recommendation is to park it. It's a long project at your employer, so it can't start this weekend, won't earn you money, and won't teach you marketing. I won't expand on it until you choose.

That's three directions and still no answers to my three questions, so here's an updated prompt for a fresh chat. It will reason better there than it can in a thread that keeps branching:

```
I'm trying to decide: which one side project I can start this weekend that earns a little money and teaches me marketing by doing it.
Context: Candidates so far are (a) a podcast about building in public and (b) a Chrome extension from ideas in my notes. [My skills: ___. Hours per week: ___. Budget: ___. Existing audience or niche: ___.]
Already decided: Nothing yet.
Ruled out, and why: Rewriting my company's backend in Rust. It's a work project, not a weekend side project, and it wouldn't earn money or teach marketing. [Confirm or change this.]
Parked for later: The podcast and the Chrome extension, whichever I don't pick. [Paste my two extension ideas here.]
What I need from you now: Pick one project and tell me why it beats the alternatives for money and marketing practice.
Lead with your recommendation, and end with a Decision and a Next step.
```

Whichever chat you use, the fastest way forward is to answer the three questions and paste your two extension ideas.
So which one do I start on Saturday?

Start the Chrome extension on Saturday. Of your options, it's the only one that can make money and teach you marketing within a few weeks.

- **Money:** An extension can charge from day one through a paid tier or a one-time price. A podcast usually takes months to build an audience before it earns anything.
- **Marketing:** Shipping one forces you to practice positioning, a store listing, a landing page, and finding your first 10 users. That's the skill you said you want.
- **Building in public:** Do it as posts about the extension instead of a podcast. You get the same story with no recording or editing overhead, and it becomes your distribution channel.

I'm inferring you can code, since you mentioned a Rust rewrite. I haven't seen your two ideas either, so the pick between them is still open.

I'd change my mind if neither idea has a user you can name and find online, or if you already have a podcast audience. In either case, tell me and I'll rethink it.

Decision: Build the Chrome extension this weekend and fold the "building in public" idea into it as posts. The podcast and the Rust rewrite stay parked.
Next step: Saturday morning, write one sentence per idea in your notes: "Who has this problem, and where can I find 10 of them?" Build the idea where you can name that place, and paste both ideas here if you want me to pick.
